message.content:
**Word Count:** ~268. Exceeds the 150–210 limit. Cut ~60 words of administrative filler to comply.

**Generic Wording:** “Beloved,” “essential maintenance work,” “ensure your weekend plans remain uninterrupted,” “popular,” and “keep our garden thriving together” are community-notice clichés. Delete subjective praise and corporate pleasantries. Deliver facts and directives in plain language.

**Artificial Transitions:** “First, please be aware that…,” “Additionally, due to…,” and “For those interested in helping…” create a rigid, bureaucratic cadence. Remove connector phrases entirely. Use spatial breaks, line breaks, or direct subheadings to separate topics instead of verbal hand-holding.

**Monotonous Rhythm:** Nearly every sentence runs 20–30 words with identical declarative structure. Combine the closure, cause, and detour into one tight sentence. Vary length with short imperatives for logistics (“Bring gloves. Tools provided.”) to break the uniform cadence and improve scanability.

**Unsupported Details:** “Monthly seed swap,” “discover new varieties,” “upcoming planting season,” “general garden upkeep this weekend,” and “dedicated volunteer coordinator” are invented. The prompt supplies only the core facts. Strip all unrequested embellishments; they bloat the notice and dilute authority.

**Actionable Fix:** Remove all filler, convert passive phrasing to active directives, align strictly with provided facts, use direct formatting for topic shifts, and compress until you hit the 150–210 range.
